name: Rosenblatt perceptron simulations on IBM 704
description: An early adaptive pattern-recognition system explored through computer simulation at Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory.

date.label: July 1958
date.basis: Date or interval stated or closely scoped by the cited source; see event caveats.

events.statement: A US Navy newsletter reported repeated IBM 704 simulations of Frank Rosenblatt’s perceptron system; dedicated hardware was still under development.
events.scope: Simulated perceptron; not the later dedicated machine
events.caveats: The source’s sweeping claims about autonomous perception are contemporary promotional claims, not evidence of general intelligence or human-level perception.

contributions.resource: Developed and simulated the perceptron under Frank Rosenblatt.

evidence.supports: The July 1958 newsletter reports repeated IBM 704 simulations, an ONR contract, and a dedicated pilot machine still under development.

events.place_note: The source locates Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory in Buffalo; it does not explicitly identify the physical location of the IBM 704 used.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest cited dated event for this scoped record; a surviving witness or publication is not itself the invention date.

places.note: Newsletter locates Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory in Buffalo.

caveats: This entry is the reported simulation capability; it does not infer the dedicated machine was complete in 1958.

research.note: Second reader inspected the July 1958 Navy newsletter via the equivalent Bitsavers mirror; technical and intelligence claims in it are not independently demonstrated by the notice.
